messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: API-GW gateway-prod is reporting a spike in 502/504 responses. 5m error rate 15% (baseline ~0.3%). Affected region: us-west-2. Root traces show increased upstream timeouts to auth-service. Pager: @aj on-call.

aj: ack — I'm on call. pulling logs and dashboards.

aj: opening the apigw error dashboard: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/apigw/errors?range=5m — seeing large fanout at edge and target deregisters.

maria: support channel reporting customers hitting 502s for POST /v1/generate. Top impacted: Acme Corp (severity: medium-high). Support tickets: #4532, #4533. Notifying customers now.

support-bot: Customer Impact Summary: 12 active sessions affected, transient errors on request retry, no PII exposure detected (audit).

samir: looking at ELB / target group — health checks for gateway-backend are showing 504s, then targets get marked unhealthy. Also seeing upstream auth timeouts ~10s. Pasting recent tails:```
[2026-03-15T10:14:02Z] gw-7f4bb ERROR upstream request failed: POST /auth/verify 504 timeout=10000ms target=10.2.7.21
[2026-03-15T10:14:03Z] gw-7f4bb WARN deregistering target 10.2.7.21 due to failed checks
[2026-03-15T10:14:10Z] gw-7f4bb ERROR fanout failed: 502 on backend pool auth-service replicas
```

samir: curl against auth-service shows slow response: `curl -v http://auth-service.us-west-2.internal/health` — long TTFB ~9s.

elaine: I see a canary rollout of model-router v2.3.1 finished at 10:05 UTC. Canary routing rate was 8% to the new router. Any correlation with auth-service?

aj: checking deploy history...confirmed canary completed at 10:05. Starting rollback of canary now (canary-only rollback).

aj: running:```
rctl deploy rollback --service=model-router --to=2.3.0 --scope=canary --reason="502 spike us-west-2"
```

ops: starting region fallback for 20% traffic from us-west-2 -> us-east-1 via routing policy `regional-fallback`. Command:```
rctl routing shift --service=api-gateway --from=us-west-2 --to=us-east-1 --percent=20 --reason="mitigation"
```

incident-bot: Action taken: canary rollback initiated; partial regional traffic shift 20% to us-east-1; circuit-breaker thresholds lowered on gateway (response timeout -> 150ms short-circuit).

samir: after rollback+shift, error rate dropped to ~4% within 90s. Still seeing some health-check churn; investigating target group timeouts.

maria: posted interim status to status.redwood.com/incidents/39321 and pinged Acme and BetaOps.

jordan: opening a runbook change: add NLB health-check timeout detection and early canary throttling rule (PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runbooks/pull/204).

elaine: quick note — auth-service metrics show a spike in request queue length around 10:12 that coincides with increased concurrency from canary. Possible connection.

aj: can we temporarily increase auth-service replicas in us-west-2 to buy headroom? samir, can you scale?

samir: scaling auth-service replicas +2 in us-west-2 now. `kctl scale deployment/auth-service --replicas=6 -n prod-us-west-2`.

ops: increased replica count and removed the handful of unhealthy targets; health checks recovering. Gateway error rate continuing down — current 5m error rate 1.2%.

aj: status update: mitigation effective. Traffic largely stable, errors below alert threshold. Keeping channel open for monitoring for 60 minutes. Postmortem owners: @samir (lead), @elaine (secondary).

maria: I'll coordinate customer follow-ups and send an executive summary once postmortem draft is ready.

jordan: assigning tasks: add NLB health-check monitor, add deploy-canary throttling rule, update runbook steps for graceful canary rollback.

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: Mitigations executed: canary rollback, regional traffic shift (20%), auth-service scale up (+2 replicas), gateway circuit-breaker tightened. Next steps: collect logs, prepare RCA, update runbook, customer comms.

aj: thanks team — if anything regresses, ping @aj and I'll re-open. Otherwise we'll transition to postmortem thread in #postmortems in 2h.

(End of thread)
